en.name: Sun-dried tomatoes in a jar
en.summary: An unopened jar of sun-dried tomatoes keeps 1 year from purchase in the cupboard. Once opened it keeps 3–6 months, whether in the cupboard or refrigerated — but with garlic or herbs in the oil, the fridge is the right choice.
en.pantry: Cool, dark and dry, 1 year from purchase unopened, and 3–6 months after opening. The tomatoes are preserved by drying and usually by salt and acid in the pack as well; the oil is there for flavour and to exclude air, not as a preservative in its own right. Keep the tomatoes fully submerged — any piece standing proud of the oil will mould — and always use a clean dry fork. If the oil clouds or solidifies in a cold kitchen, that is the olive oil setting and it clears on warming.
en.fridge: Refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, an opened jar also keeps 3–6 months, and there are good reasons to prefer the fridge. Many jars contain garlic, basil or other fresh aromatics in the oil, and low-acid vegetables held under oil at room temperature are the situation that produces botulism toxin; refrigeration is the practical household control for that, together with using the jar within its window. Expect the oil to go cloudy and thick in the cold — stand the jar out for a few minutes before serving and it clears.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for jarred sun-dried tomatoes, and freezing is a poor fit. Oil does not freeze cleanly, it separates and goes waxy, and the tomatoes themselves are already dried and dense so they gain nothing. If you have a surplus, the better move is to blitz the tomatoes with their oil into a paste or pesto and freeze that in small portions, where the texture change does not matter.
en.thawing: If you have frozen a tomato paste or pesto, thaw it in the fridge and stir the separated oil back in before use.
spoilage: Mould at the surface, usually on a piece sitting above the oil.
A rancid, crayon-like smell from oil that has oxidised.
Fermented, fizzy or yeasty smell, or bubbles rising in the jar.
Tomatoes that have gone slimy, or oil that has turned ropy.
tips: Push the tomatoes back under the oil after every use.
Use a clean dry fork, never fingers.
Refrigerate an opened jar if it contains garlic or fresh herbs.
Save the flavoured oil for dressings and pasta — but keep enough to cover the tomatoes.

faq.q: How long do sun-dried tomatoes in oil keep after opening?
faq.a: 3–6 months, in the cupboard or the fridge. Refrigerate if the jar contains garlic or fresh herbs.

faq.q: Do they have to be refrigerated once opened?
faq.a: The window is the same either way, but the fridge is the safer choice for any jar with garlic or fresh aromatics in the oil.

faq.q: Why has the oil gone cloudy in the fridge?
faq.a: Olive oil solidifies when cold. It is not spoilage — leave the jar at room temperature for a few minutes and it clears.

zh.name: 油漬番茄乾
zh.summary: 未開封的油漬番茄乾從購買日起算放櫥櫃可放 1 年。開封後不論放櫥櫃或冷藏都是 3～6 個月——但如果油裡有大蒜或香草，冷藏才是正確選擇。
zh.pantry: 陰涼、避光、乾燥：未開封自購買日起 1 年，開封後 3～6 個月。番茄靠乾燥保存，通常再加上包裝裡的鹽與酸；油是為了風味與隔絕空氣，本身不是防腐劑。請讓番茄完全浸在油面下，任何露出來的那一片都會最先長霉；也一律使用乾淨乾燥的叉子。天冷時油變混濁或凝固，那是橄欖油的正常現象，回溫就會清澈。
zh.fridge: 冷藏在 4 °C 以下，開封後同樣是 3～6 個月，而且有充分理由選冷藏。很多產品的油裡放了大蒜、羅勒或其他新鮮香料，而「低酸性蔬菜在室溫下泡在油裡」正是會產生肉毒桿菌毒素的情境；冷藏就是家庭層級最實際的控制手段，再加上在期限內用完。低溫下油會變濁變稠——上桌前把罐子放室溫幾分鐘就會恢復。
zh.freezer: 油漬番茄乾沒有公布的冷凍期限，而且冷凍並不適合。油沒辦法乾淨地結凍，會分離、變得像蠟；番茄本身又已經乾燥緊實，冷凍得不到什麼。如果量太多，比較好的做法是連油一起打成番茄醬或青醬，再分小份冷凍——那時候質地變化就無所謂了。
zh.thawing: 如果冷凍的是番茄醬或醬料，請放冷藏解凍，使用前把分離的油攪回去。
spoilage: 表面長霉，通常長在露出油面的那一片。
油氧化後發出油耗味或蠟筆味。
有發酵味、氣泡感或酵母味，或罐中不斷冒泡。
番茄變黏滑，或油變得牽絲。
tips: 每次用完把番茄壓回油面下。
使用乾淨乾燥的叉子，不要用手。
罐子裡有大蒜或新鮮香草的，開封後就冷藏。
香料油留著做油醋或拌麵，但要留足以蓋過番茄的量。

faq.q: 油漬番茄乾開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 放櫥櫃或冷藏都是 3～6 個月。含大蒜或新鮮香草的請冷藏。
兩邊的期限一樣，但只要油裡有大蒜或新鮮香料，冷藏就是比較安全的選擇。

faq.q: 油在冰箱裡變白濁是壞了嗎？
faq.a: 不是。橄欖油低溫會凝固，放室溫幾分鐘就會恢復清澈。
